clue.text: Labour restriction

definitions.meaning: labour in the sense of childbirth, the old term for the lying-in period
being shut in or kept within limits

explanation.definitionFit: Childbirth was traditionally called a woman's lying-in, and the word also means imprisonment or being shut in.

clue.text: Rudolf's North American cousin?

parts.note: Rudolf the red-nosed reindeer's relative living in Canada or Alaska

explanation.definitionFit: The North American wild reindeer is a close relative of the reindeer of the Christmas song.

clue.text: Cash registers?

definitions.meaning: as a verb, records or remarks upon something

explanation.definitionFit: Paper money is called banknotes, and to note something is to register or record it.

clue.text: Puck is given the push in this

definitions.text: Puck is given the push in this

parts.words: Puck is given the push in this
parts.note: Puck looks like Shakespeare's sprite being sacked, but it is the rubber disc shoved along the rink

explanation.definitionFit: The winter team sport played on a rink with sticks propels a hard rubber disc.

clue.text: Boy in a whirl

definitions.meaning: a boy's name, a short form of Edward
a swirling current of water or air

explanation.definitionFit: It is a familiar boy's name and also a small whirlpool or circular current.

clue.text: Engaged, that's the outcome about me and a girl

indicators.note: the outcome goes about, that is around, the other pieces

parts.note: the end of something is its outcome
taken as written
she stands for any female, a girl

explanation.surface: Someone engaged is told the result concerns them and a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged' reads as betrothed, fitting the girl, but it means meshed like gears. 'that's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmeshed means caught up or entangled, in the sense of engaged like interlocking gears.

clue.text: Time of strain?

parts.note: strain looks like stress, but it is a musical strain or melody, whose speed is its time

explanation.definitionFit: In music the speed or pace of a piece is its time, the Italian term for the beat rate.

clue.text: Balance to settle around mid-January

indicators.note: to settle goes around the middle piece

parts.note: to reside somewhere is to settle and live there
U is the middle letter of the seven-letter word January

explanation.surface: An account is to be squared by the middle of January.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts RESIDE round U, the centre letter of JANUARY: RESID-U-E.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what remains, the balance left over after the rest is taken.

clue.text: Section making up part of a personal column

definitions.text: Section making up part of a personal column

parts.words: Section making up part of a personal column
parts.note: the personal column looks like newspaper small ads, but it is a person's spinal column

explanation.definitionFit: Each of the small bones linked to form the backbone is one segment of the spinal column.

clue.text: Dutch city bank headed by a rascal

parts.note: a rotter is an old-fashioned word for a cad or rascal
a dam is an embankment holding back water

explanation.surface: A Dutch port's riverside is led by some scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headed by' means the rascal comes first, before the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam is the great port city of the Netherlands, an example of a Dutch city.

clue.text: Hunts -with seeming success

definitions.meaning: fox-hunting gatherings are called ..., so hunts as nouns
the phrase ... with success, read with the dash as a continuation

explanation.definitionFit: A hunting gathering is called a meet, and one who succeeds is said to meet with success.

clue.text: Twice jump over a piece on board

parts.note: bis is the Latin-derived musical marking meaning twice
to hop is to make a little jump

explanation.surface: Leaping twice over a draughts piece on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS, meaning twice or encore, is a crossword staple. 'over' simply means the first piece goes on top of the second in this down-the-page reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The bishop is one of the chessmen, a piece moved on the chess board.

clue.text: Various designs to a dress

indicators.note: to design is to plan a new arrangement, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Different patterns for making up a frock.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted goods are mixed and of several kinds, a synonym of various.

clue.text: Clever people are quick on it

definitions.text: Clever people are quick on it

parts.words: Clever people are quick on it
parts.note: bright people are described as quick in understanding, using the idiom quick on the ...

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says intelligent people are quick to grasp things, the noun meaning comprehension.

clue.text: It can yet conceal firmness of purpose

indicators.note: the true word is concealed in a disguised arrangement of these letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Resolve may still be able to be kept hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceal' tells you ITCANYET is a disguised arrangement of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacity is persistence and determination, holding fast to an aim.

clue.text: King and prophet can be dependable

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king
Eli was the priest and prophet who raised Samuel in the Old Testament
to be able is to be capable, so can means able

explanation.surface: A monarch and a seer may be trustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reliable can be trusted to work, a direct synonym of dependable.

clue.text: Viral disease took off, we hear, in its abbreviated form

definitions.text: Viral disease took off, we hear, in its abbreviated form

parts.words: Viral disease took off, we hear, in its abbreviated form
parts.note: a word sounding like flew, meaning took off, is the short name of this viral illness

explanation.definitionFit: The full name of the common viral illness is shortened to a word that sounds like flew.

clue.text: Switched round the spot dance, there's a pattern to it

indicators.note: the two pieces are swapped from the order in which the clue gives them

parts.note: the polka is a lively Bohemian dance
a dot is a spot

explanation.surface: Spinning around on one spot in a dance follows a routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the spot first and the dance second; 'Switched round' swaps them.
explanation.definitionFit: A design of regularly spaced round spots on fabric is a familiar pattern.

clue.text: Poet writes new sonnet about New York

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, that is around, the abbreviation
a new version of the word is a fresh arrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet composes a fresh sonnet about New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like part of New York or a fresh poem, but it signals the rearrangement; 'writes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was the Victorian Poet Laureate, an example of a poet.

clue.text: Not unwilling to try a tea break

parts.note: to try something out is to test it

indicators.note: breaking the word up lets its letters be reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Keen to attempt a pause for a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges TEA to ATE. 'Not unwilling' really means having left a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies testate has made a valid will, so is literally not without a will.

clue.text: A very strong atmosphere of romance

parts.note: ff is the musical marking fortissimo, very loud or strong
an air is an atmosphere or ambience around something

explanation.surface: A powerful aura of love surrounds someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very strong' is the music sign ff (fortissimo).
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair is a romantic relationship, so the word stands for a romance.

clue.text: Communist leader is a flaming capitalist

parts.note: Red is a common nickname for a communist
a head is a leader or chief

explanation.surface: The party boss turns out to be a fiery money-man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a flaming capitalist' is a person with a flame-coloured top, the capital being the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with fiery red hair has a flaming top, punningly a flaming head, hence capitalist.

clue.text: An example of ill, humour?

parts.note: read without the comma it is ill humour; with it, humour that is sick or in bad taste

explanation.definitionFit: A joke in poor taste about death or disease is called sick, so it is ill humour.

clue.text: He tries to do his job

definitions.text: He tries to do his job

parts.words: He tries to do his job
parts.note: tries looks like makes an effort, but it means hears court cases

explanation.definitionFit: A court official who presides over trials is the one whose work is trying cases.

clue.text: Rotten place to clear out

parts.note: to place something is to put it
to rid a room is to clear it out

explanation.definitionFit: Putrid food is decomposing and foul, a synonym of rotten.

clue.text: Dispute arrest

definitions.meaning: a quarrel or clash with someone
to take someone into custody, in police slang

explanation.definitionFit: A brush with someone is a quarrel, and the phrasal verb also means to arrest a suspect.

clue.text: Arab prince appears in a strange mirage

indicators.note: the answer appears inside the run of letters of the words given

explanation.surface: An Arab ruler shows up in an odd desert illusion.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or prince, especially in Arab lands.

clue.text: Bill and Edward took part

parts.note: a bill is an account, abbreviated AC
Ted is a familiar short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Bill and Edward both played a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name alongside Edward, but it is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in a play is to take part in it, a theatrical synonym.

clue.text: Catholic dignitary in a northern church has a commanding position

parts.note: Dom is a title given to some Catholic, especially Benedictine, monks and clergy
taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A Catholic cleric in a church up north holds a powerful post.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominance is supremacy or control, the state of holding a commanding position.

clue.text: Possibly treated nine to dinner?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters can be put into another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A host perhaps paid for a dinner for nine guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges TREATED and NINE together; the whole clue also describes a host feeding guests.
explanation.definitionFit: To give guests a meal is to host them, so treating nine people to dinner is hosting them.
